title: Speed, Distance, Time: The Travel Triangle

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: The Physics of Motion
blocks.content: How long will a road trip take? How fast must a rocket fly to reach the moon in 3 days? All of these massive physics problems boil down to one beautiful, unbreakable relationship between three variables: **Speed, Distance, and Time (SDT)**. If you know any two of them, you can instantly find the third!

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Magic Triangle
blocks.content:
You don't need to memorize three different formulas; you just need to draw the Magic Triangle!

• Draw a triangle. Put **D (Distance)** at the very top point.
• Put **S (Speed)** and **T (Time)** next to each other at the bottom.
• cover up the letter you want to find with your thumb.
• If the two remaining letters are one over the other (D over T), you DIVIDE.
• If the two remaining letters are next to each other (S next to T), you MULTIPLY.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: The Decimal Time Trap
blocks.content:
The math is easy, but the TIME units are deadly!

1. If you calculate a time and get **2.5 hours**, this does NOT mean 2 hours and 50 minutes!
2. There are 60 minutes in an hour, not 100. So 0.5 hours means *half* an hour (30 minutes).
3. **To convert decimal hours into minutes:** Always multiply the decimal part by 60! (e.g., 0.2 hours × 60 = 12 minutes).

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Finding the Speed
blocks.content:
A train travels 240 kilometers. The journey takes 3 hours and 15 minutes. Find the average speed in km/h.

• **Step 1 (Fix the Time):** We cannot use 3.15! 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour (15/60 = 0.25). So the time is actually **3.25 hours**.
• **Step 2 (The Triangle):** We want Speed. Cover 'S'. We are left with D over T. (Distance ÷ Time).
• **Step 3 (Plug in):** Speed = 240 ÷ 3.25
• **Step 4 (Calculate):** 240 ÷ 3.25 = 73.846...

**Final Answer: 73.8 km/h (1 d.p.)**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The most brutal trap is calculating **Average Speed** for a multi-part journey. If you drive to a city at 100km/h and drive back at 50km/h, your average speed is NOT 75km/h! (You spent way more time driving slowly on the way back, so the average drops lower). You CANNOT just average the two speeds. You MUST calculate the **Total Distance** of the whole trip, and divide it by the **Total Time** of the whole trip. Always!
